data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"A panel of non-experts following a checklist is more reliable than a single expert because it transforms the judgment task from a 'pattern recognition' problem into a 'distributed search' problem, effectively eliminating the expert's single-point-of-failure bias.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The task requires synthesis of contradictory evidence rather than a binary check of presence/absence.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The checklist is written by the same expert whose intuition it seeks to replace, thereby encoding the same biases.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The panel exhibits strong groupthink, leading to a 'social' single-point-of-failure.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The expert relies on high-dimensional heuristics (intuition) which are prone to 'availability bias' or 'overfitting' to past cases. The checklist forces a serial, exhaustive search of the problem space. The panel structure ensures that the 'cost' of missing a checklist item is distributed; the probability that all panel members overlook a mandatory check is exponentially lower than the probability of a single expert having a blind spot.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
